title: Reglas 1 y 2: género y los artículos el, la, los, las
summary: Nouns have a gender. 'The' has four forms that must match the noun.
instruction: Which article agrees with the noun?
explanation: Rule 1: Nouns in Spanish have genders. They are either masculine or feminine. The word for car is carro. It is masculine. Notice it ends in an o. Many (not all) masculine words end in o. The word for house, casa, is feminine. Notice it ends in an a. Many (not all) feminine words end in a.
To make words plural you usually add an s, or es if the noun ends in a consonant.
Rule 2: In English there is only one word for 'the'. In Spanish there are four. The definite article changes depending on whether the noun is singular or plural, masculine or feminine.
el = the (masculine, singular) · la = the (feminine, singular) · los = the (masculine, plural) · las = the (feminine, plural)
